newsitem.title: ITALY: Top Italian state rail executive arrested - media.
newsitem.headline: Top Italian state rail executive arrested - media.

text.p: Police have arrested the managing director of Italy's state railway system, Lorenzo Necci, media reports quoting judicial sources said on Monday.
Italian television and news agencies said Necci, 55, had been arrested on Sunday on a warrant from magistrates in the town of La Spezia on the Ligurian coast in northwest Italy.
A spokesman for the railway, Ferrovie dello Stato, said he could not confirm the reports.
The news agency AGI, quoting judicial sources, said Necci was being held on suspicion of offences which included corruption and abuse of office. It gave no further details.

Necci, who has worked at the railway in various positions since 1990, had been overseeing a plan to launch a multi-billion dollar high-speed railway which, when it gets off the ground, is expected to be one of Europe's largest construction projects.
A trade union leader who worked closely with Necci said he was surprised to hear the reports about Necci's arrest, adding he was worried about how it would affect the high-speed project.
"I'm shocked," said Paolo Brutti, secretary general of the FILT-CIGL union representing railway workers.
"For the unions, Necci's arrest was a surprise, but also the source of great worry for the launch of major works on the railway infrastructure and the modernisation of the system."
AGI reported that two Italian businessmen also had been arrested in the same investigation.
